voices.name: v1_deep_male
voices.instruct: Male, mid-40s, deep warm baritone, American English. Calm, confident documentary narrator, like a premium nature film. Unhurried pace with natural pauses, a subtle sense of wonder and intrigue. Close-mic studio recording.

voices.name: v2_british_male
voices.instruct: Male, 50s, rich British English accent, velvety and authoritative documentary narrator. Measured, slow pace, gentle gravitas, slightly hushed when revealing a surprising fact. Close-mic studio recording.

voices.name: v3_warm_female
voices.instruct: Female, mid-30s, warm low-pitched American English voice. Intimate, curious storytelling tone of a travel documentary narrator. Relaxed pace, a hint of a smile on surprising facts. Close-mic studio recording.

ref_text: Some places on Earth were never meant for people. And yet, people found a way to live there anyway.
text:
A polar bear walks down the main street. A pregnant woman packs her bags and boards a plane, because no baby is born in this town. And on the hill above the houses, there is a cemetery that stopped taking the dead seventy-five years ago.
This is Longyearbyen. The northernmost town on Earth. You can't be born here. You can't be buried here. And yet more than two thousand people refuse to leave.
By the end of this video, you'll understand why.
